topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture by outlining the learning objectives and setting the framework for understanding cancer as an evolutionary process.

topics.label: Genetic and epigenetic drivers of clonal evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer evolves through the Darwinian selection of genetically mutated clones and non-mutational epigenetic alterations that confer growth advantages.

topics.label: Cell of origin and cancer stem cell hierarchy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the cancer stem cell model and present experimental evidence for how tissue hierarchies and specific cells of origin influence tumor initiation.

topics.label: Microenvironmental and inflammatory promotion of tumor growth
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how environmental promoters, chronic inflammation, and supportive stroma create permissive conditions that drive cancer progression.

topics.label: Methods for investigating tumor evolution and spatial heterogeneity
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the experimental technologies and computational tools used to map clonal evolution and cellular interactions within tumors.

topics.label: Integrative evolutionary model of cancer progression
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic synthesizes the interplay among mutational accumulation, cellular origin, and microenvironmental cues into a unified model of cancer development.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next session preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture and previews the upcoming session on cancer therapies.
